score_rationale: Solid willingness-to-pay validated by commercial market: at least 5 vendors (Dietrich Direct, IT NOW Technologies, Bancomail, InfoGlobalData, Exact Data) currently selling funeral director databases ranging from 4,338 to 9,738+ records with pricing from $69 baseline (Dietrich Direct funeral director database at $69 represents lower price point than other professional license databases, suggesting moderate but not exceptional willingness-to-pay). Three primary B2B buyer segments: (1) funeral supply vendors and casket/urn manufacturers (Batesville Casket Company, Matthews International, Aurora Casket, York Group, Trigard) selling caskets, urns, embalming tables, preparation room equipment, and funeral service supplies to funeral homes — funeral supply vendors pay $2,000-$5,000/year for funeral director prospect lists to sell products with $500-$5,000 per-funeral-home annual spend; (2) funeral home management software vendors (Frazer Consultants, FrontRunner, CFS Funeral Software, HMIS Mortuary Software, Passare) selling preneed management systems, mortuary operations software, obituary publishing platforms, and cremation tracking tools at $100-$400/month per funeral home ($1,200-$4,800/year LTV) — software vendors pay $3,000-$8,000/year for funeral director marketing lists; and (3) continuing education providers selling mandatory state-required CE courses — funeral directors in most states must complete 3-12 hours of continuing education annually or biennially to maintain license renewal (California requires 8 hours biennially, Texas requires 6 hours annually, Florida requires 12 hours biennially), creating recurring $100-$300 per funeral director spend on accredited CE content. All 51 jurisdictions (50 states + DC) require funeral director licensing as of 2026 (confirmed by GetLicenseMap state comparison and The International Conference of Funeral Service Examining Boards). State Boards of Funeral Service or Departments of Professional Regulation maintain public funeral director license registries accessible through state-specific websites and aggregated via The International Conference's Look Up a License tool at theconferenceonline.org. Data includes funeral director full name, license number, license status (active, inactive, suspended, revoked), initial licensure date, firm affiliation/funeral home name (where listed), business address (availability varies by state), and disciplinary history (public actions only). Zero PII — all professional credential and disciplinary data under state funeral service practice acts and freedom of information laws. Engineering lift is moderate: scrape from 51 state funeral service boards (Texas TFSC, Mississippi MSBFS, Pennsylvania State Board, Georgia Board confirmed publicly searchable) plus The International Conference national lookup, deduplicate multi-jurisdiction licenses, normalize status codes and firm affiliations. No affordable flat-file competitor exists on Gumroad or similar marketplaces, though baseline commercial pricing is lower ($69 Dietrich Direct vs. $200+ for engineers/attorneys), suggesting moderate willingness-to-pay tier. Audience size is modest: approximately 30,000-40,000 licensed funeral directors nationwide (19,136 funeral homes in NFDA 2021 report, typically 1-3 licensed directors per home), creating a TAM of 1,000-2,000 potential B2B buyers across funeral supplies, software, and CE providers. Score is 7 due to validated willingness-to-pay from multiple commercial vendors but at lower baseline pricing ($69-$200 range vs. $200-$300 for higher-scoring professions), confirmed public data availability across all 51 jurisdictions with national aggregation via The International Conference, absence of low-cost flat-file alternatives, modest but stable funeral director population (30K-40K), and three distinct B2B buyer segments with proven purchasing behavior in funeral services industry.

data_wanted: All 51 U.S. jurisdictions (50 states + DC) require funeral director licensing as of 2026 (confirmed by GetLicenseMap comprehensive state comparison). State Boards of Funeral Service, State Boards of Embalmers and Funeral Directors, or Departments of Professional Regulation maintain public funeral director license registries accessible through state-specific websites, with national aggregation available via The International Conference of Funeral Service Examining Boards' Look Up a License tool at theconferenceonline.org. Texas Funeral Service Commission (TFSC at tfsc.texas.gov with online verification), Mississippi State Board of Funeral Service (MSBFS with license verification search), Pennsylvania State Board of Funeral Directors, Georgia State Board of Funeral Service, and 47 additional state boards all provide public searchable databases. Funeral director licensing requires mortuary science education from ABFSE-accredited program and passing the National Board Examination (NBE) administered by The International Conference. Key fields per license: funeral director full name (first, middle initial, last), state license number (format varies by state, typically alphanumeric 4-8 characters), initial licensure date (date of first funeral director license issuance in that state), license expiration/renewal date (where publicly listed), license status (active, inactive, suspended, revoked), funeral home affiliation or establishment name (where listed by state board — many states require funeral directors to report current employer), business address (street, city, state, ZIP — availability varies by state based on public records policies and funeral director privacy elections), embalmer license (where applicable — some states issue separate embalmer credentials, others combine funeral director/embalmer into single license), and disciplinary history (public disciplinary actions, suspensions, and revocations — private warnings not included). Target all active licenses (optionally include inactive for premium tier). Scope to individual funeral directors only — exclude funeral home establishments or unlicensed funeral service personnel. Approximately 30,000-40,000 licensed funeral directors nationwide as of 2026 (estimated from 19,136 funeral homes per NFDA 2021 report with typical 1-3 licensed directors per establishment). Target output: 35K rows, one per license. Data is 100% public per state funeral service practice acts and state Freedom of Information laws — funeral director licensing and disciplinary records are public information under state mortuary science statutes.
